name: Malcolm Garrett
life: “I still remember cleaning a steering wheel I still couldn't afford to learn on.” On Saturday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Malcolm knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I paid for my license by cleaning the instructor's flat. I don't want to send another learner to scrub a floor.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a soft blue checked shirt and a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead. Malcolm has a small notch in the left eyebrow, with a loose dark braid. Malcolm counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices during a conversation.
personality: Malcolm uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Malcolm well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To provide a funded lesson without unpaid labor in exchange.
family: Maria Dias is Malcolm’s second cousin. Malcolm gets to change the plan. Maria offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The third bedroom*, Maria says, “I can rent a room to the lodger but I have a noisy night shift.”
connections: Parker Gao. A free lesson starts with hearing an honest question about eyesight. Also in the story is Gareth Mercer (funded learner).

reactions.situation: Two people qualify for the same funded lesson
reactions.response: Malcolm asks both applicants which transport difficulty one lesson would actually address.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Malcolm asks the stranger who will be expecting them, then helps find a way to tell that person.
